MAINT-TIMEOUT-S1.title: Define Timeout UX State Schema and Contract
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S1.description: Define frontend state model for long-running request handling including explicit 45s timeout threshold, modal trigger condition, user decision (continue/abandon), resumed_request_id linkage, and request lifecycle states (pending, timed_out, resumed, cancelled).

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S2.title: Implement Timeout Detection and Control Logic
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S2.description: Implement core logic using timers and AbortController to detect long-running requests (~45s), trigger timeout state, pause UI updates, ensure proper AbortController reuse vs re-init, and guarantee timer cleanup on unmount with continuation and cancellation paths.

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S3.title: Render Timeout Modal with Continue/Abandon UX
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S3.description: Build and refine modal UI that appears on timeout, providing clear options to continue waiting or abandon the request, including accessibility features (focus trap, keyboard navigation) and explicit UX messaging for long-running uncertainty.

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S4.title: Integrate Timeout Handling with Chat Request Flow
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S4.description: Integrate timeout logic into end-to-end chat flow ensuring resumed requests continue correctly without duplicate backend calls, cancelled requests clean up state, and UI enforces idempotent handling with no orphaned or duplicated responses.

MAINT-TIMEOUT-S5.title: Unit and Interaction Tests for Timeout UX
MAINT-TIMEOUT-S5.description: Create tests covering timeout trigger timing, modal display, continue/abandon actions, AbortController behavior, prevention of duplicate responses after resume, and edge cases such as rapid successive timeouts and mid-response user decisions.
